title: The pullback of a descent datum along the diagonal is the identity
statement: Let $X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $V$ be a scheme over $X$, and let $\varphi:\mathrm{pr}_0^*V\to\mathrm{pr}_1^*V$ be a descent datum on $V$ over $X/Y$ [def-pd-descent-datum], where $\mathrm{pr}_0,\mathrm{pr}_1:X\times_YX\to X$ are the projections of the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $\Delta:X\to X\times_YX$ be the diagonal, the morphism with $\mathrm{pr}_0\circ\Delta=\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\Delta=\mathrm{id}_X$. Since $\mathrm{pr}_k\circ\Delta=\mathrm{id}_X$, the pullbacks $\Delta^*\mathrm{pr}_0^*V$ and $\Delta^*\mathrm{pr}_1^*V$ are both canonically identified with $V$ as schemes over $X$; under these identifications the pullback $\Delta^*\varphi:V\to V$ of $\varphi$ along $\Delta$ equals $\mathrm{id}_V$.

source.place: Descent, Section 35.34, paragraph following Definition 35.34.1 (Tag 023V): 'In fact, $\Delta^*\varphi$ is equal to the identity' (descent.tex line 8143)

proof.text: By the universal property of the fibre product, the diagonal $\Delta:X\to X\times_YX$ is the unique map whose two composites with the projections are both $\mathrm{id}_X$. Pulling back the descent datum along the diagonal therefore identifies each of $\Delta^*\mathrm{pr}_0^*V$ and $\Delta^*\mathrm{pr}_1^*V$ with $V$ over $X$.

source.place: Descent, Definition Tag 023V (line 8101) and the paragraph immediately following it (line 8143)

proof.text: Pull back the cocycle identity for $\varphi$ along the triple diagonal $\delta:X\to X\times_YX\times_YX$; by the universal property of the fibre product, $\mathrm{pr}_{01}\circ\delta=\mathrm{pr}_{02}\circ\delta=\mathrm{pr}_{12}\circ\delta=\Delta$. Under the canonical identifications from Step 1, all three pullbacks of $\varphi$ are the same endomorphism $e:=\Delta^*\varphi$ of $V$, so the cocycle gives $e=e\circ e$. Since $\varphi$ is an isomorphism by the definition of a descent datum, $e$ is an isomorphism; composing the equality on the left with $e^{-1}$ yields $\mathrm{id}_V=e$, which is the asserted identity.
